title: Practice 7: Setting out: пойти, поехать — and сходить, съездить

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Ты не ___ (поехать — to set off (by vehicle)) в Боснию на каникулы.
exercises.why: **поедешь** is the future tense (2nd person singular) of **поехать** (to go (in a conveyance or on horseback)) — the perfective of **ехать**, «set out». future: я пое́ду · ты пое́дешь · он пое́дет · мы пое́дем · вы пое́дете · они пое́дут. — Wiktionary, «поехать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The future perfective (поеду, поедешь) belongs to the 1st -е- type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «ехать — ездить: perfective поехать · «for a while» поездить · «round trip» съездить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Мы поездили по городу и поехали домой.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: You aren't going to Bosnia on vacation.
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: Я ___ (сплавать — to swim there and back) до другого конца бассейна.
exercises.why: **сплавал** is the past tense (masculine) of **сплавать** — the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back. — Wiktionary, «сплавать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «b) Prefix "с-" implying a single round trip. The prefix "с-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: сходить, съездить, слетать. These verbs denote a single trip (going to and coming from a place), especially when a quick return is implied.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: I swam to the other end of the pool and back.
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: Я всегда хотел ___ (поездить — to ride about for a while) по Европе.
exercises.why: **поездить** (the infinitive) (to go (by horse or vehicle), to ride, to drive) — the perfective of **ездить** meaning «for a while». — Wiktionary, «поездить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «a) Prefix "по-" denoting a perfective action of limited duration (an action "for a while"). The prefix "по-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: походить, поездить, полетать. These verbs denote a single completed action of limited duration, similar to the verb "погулять".» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «ехать — ездить: perfective поехать · «for a while» поездить · «round trip» съездить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Мы поездили по городу и поехали домой.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: I've always wanted to travel through Europe.
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: Неискренний подарок впрок не ___ (пойти — to go, set off (on foot)).
exercises.why: **пойдёт** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **пойти** (to go) — the perfective of **йти**, «set out». future: я пойду́ · ты пойдёшь · он пойдёт · мы пойдём · вы пойдёте · они пойду́т. — Wiktionary, «пойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «Note. — that the vowel -ё- in the verb "пойти" occurs in the masculine form only: пошёл, пошла, пошло, пошли. The future perfective (пойду, пойдёшь) belongs to the 1st -ё- type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Она пошла в библиотеку.» (She went to (left for) the library.) — DLI, Lesson 54. «После завтрака они пойдут в магазин.» (After breakfast they will go to (leave for) the store.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: One won't profit by an insincere gift.
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: Я сегодня ___ (сходить — to go and come back (on foot)) в океанариум.
exercises.why: **сходил** is the past tense (masculine) of **сходить** (to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off) — the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back. past: он сходи́л · она сходи́ла · оно сходи́ло · они сходи́ли. — Wiktionary, «сходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «b) Prefix "с-" implying a single round trip. The prefix "с-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: сходить, съездить, слетать. These verbs denote a single trip (going to and coming from a place), especially when a quick return is implied.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Он сходил к другу.» (He went to a friend's place (and has returned; see prefixed perfective forms of motion verbs below).) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Мне надо сходить на почту за письмами.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: I went to the aquarium today.
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: Недалёк тот день, когда мы сможем ___ (полететь — to fly off) на Марс.
exercises.why: **полететь** (the infinitive) (to fly, to be flying) — the perfective of **лететь**, «set out». — Wiktionary, «полететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The perfective verb полететь (like пойти and поехать) denotes single action with the emphasis on the completed start. The past perfective (полетел, -ла, -ло, -ли) is formed in a regular way. The future perfective (полечу, полетишь) belongs to the 2nd (-и-) type of conjugation. The consonant "т" changes into "ч" in the first person singular only.» — DLI, Lesson 55.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «лететь — летать: perfective полететь · «for a while» полетать · «round trip» слетать.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Полковник полетел в Вашингтон.» (The Colonel flew to Washington. (single action; completed start)) — DLI, Lesson 55. «Завтра я полечу на фронт.» (Tomorrow I'll fly to the front. (single action)) — DLI, Lesson 55.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: It won't be long before we can travel to Mars.
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: The branch began to bend as I climbed along it.
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: Я ___ (съездить — to go and come back (by vehicle)) на однодневную экскурсию.
exercises.why: **съездил** is the past tense (masculine) of **съездить** (to go somewhere and come back, to fetch something/to pick up someone (by a vehicle) [with за (za, + accusative) ‘somewhere’]) — the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back. past: он съе́здил · она съе́здила · оно съе́здило · они съе́здили. — Wiktionary, «съездить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «b) Prefix "с-" implying a single round trip. exercises.q: I only meant to buy one gift, but I got carried away and bought half the store.
exercises.why: **понесло** is the past tense (neuter) of **понести** (to carry (for a while) — the perfective of **нести**, «set out». past: он понёс · она понесла́ · оно понесло́ · они понесли́. — Wiktionary, «понести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **несло** is a form of **нести** (to bear, to bring, to carry); **носило** is a form of **носить** (to carry, to bear (a burden)).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.ru: Я собиралась купить только один подарок, но меня ___, и я скупила полмагазина.
exercises.context: Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite). (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Том ___ (съездить — to go and come back (by vehicle)) на однодневную экскурсию.
exercises.why: **съездил** is the past tense (masculine) of **съездить** (to go somewhere and come back, to fetch something/to pick up someone (by a vehicle) [with за (za, + accusative) ‘somewhere’]) — the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back. past: он съе́здил · она съе́здила · оно съе́здило · они съе́здили. — Wiktionary, «съездить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «b) Prefix "с-" implying a single round trip. The prefix "с-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: сходить, съездить, слетать. These verbs denote a single trip (going to and coming from a place), especially when a quick return is implied.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «ехать — ездить: perfective поехать · «for a while» поездить · «round trip» съездить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Я съезжу на вокзал и узнаю, когда отходит поезд.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: После неловкой паузы Билл взял ее за руку и ___ (потащить — to drag off) наверх.
exercises.why: **потащил** is the past tense (masculine) of **потащить** (to start pulling) — the perfective of **тащить**, «set out». past: он потащи́л · она потащи́ла · оно потащи́ло · они потащи́ли. — Wiktionary, «потащить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: After an awkward pause, Bill took her by the hand and dragged her upstairs.
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: ___ (сходить — to go and come back (on foot)) в хозяйственный магазин и купи шурупов.
exercises.why: **сходи** is the imperative (ты, singular) of **сходить** (to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off) — the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back. imperative: сходи́ · сходи́те. — Wiktionary, «сходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «b) Prefix "с-" implying a single round trip. The prefix "с-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: сходить, съездить, слетать. These verbs denote a single trip (going to and coming from a place), especially when a quick return is implied.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Он сходил к другу.» (He went to a friend's place (and has returned; see prefixed perfective forms of motion verbs below).) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Мне надо сходить на почту за письмами.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Go to the hardware store and get screws.
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: Отец никогда тебя не простит, если ты ___ (пойти — to go, set off (on foot)) в спецназ.
exercises.why: **пойдёшь** is the future tense (2nd person singular) of **пойти** (to go) — the perfective of **йти**, «set out». future: я пойду́ · ты пойдёшь · он пойдёт · мы пойдём · вы пойдёте · они пойду́т. — Wiktionary, «пойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «Note. — that the vowel -ё- in the verb "пойти" occurs in the masculine form only: пошёл, пошла, пошло, пошли. The future perfective (пойду, пойдёшь) belongs to the 1st -ё- type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Она пошла в библиотеку.» (She went to (left for) the library.) — DLI, Lesson 54. «После завтрака они пойдут в магазин.» (After breakfast they will go to (leave for) the store.) — DLI, Lesson 54.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
